children: Japan's rate reset matters beyond its borders as competition for capital intensifies, BlackRock strategists say in a research note. The strategists reckon that there is a feedback loop across bond markets: "higher U.S. rates could weaken the yen and pressure the BOJ to move faster, while higher Japanese rates could draw more capital home, weakening demand for Treasurys and pushing U.S. borrowing costs higher." Decades of ultralow domestic yields have made Japan a major exporter for capital, currently holding roughly $1.1 trillion of U.S. Treasurys, they note. A 5% repatriation by Japanese investors would amount to $55 billion--equivalent to roughly a quarter of the increase in total foreign Treasury holdings last year, they note. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
